newsitem.title: USA: JonBenet Ramsey's parents deny role in her murder.
newsitem.headline: JonBenet Ramsey's parents deny role in her murder.

text.p: The parents of JonBenet Ramsey denied Thursday they murdered their daughter and pledged to track down the killer of the 6-year-old beauty pageant contestant.
At a secretly arranged news conference with select members of the local media, John and Patricia Ramsey also said rumours their daughter was sexually molested were "totaly false."
"I did not kill my daughter JonBenet," John Ramsey said. "I will miss her dearly for the rest of my life."

The girl's body was found Dec. 26, 1996, by her father in the basement of the family's home, about eight hours after her mother said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000. No arrests have been made and no suspects named.
An autopsy said the girl may have been sexually abused.

The Ramseys have been targets of the investigation amid widespread speculation they may have played a role in the murder. Until Wednesday, when they answered questions from the police, they had declined to be interviewed by investigators.
Patricia Ramsey, her voice cracking, denied murdering her daughter and said she would not rest until police found the real killer.
"I did not kill JonBenet," she said. "I did not have anything to do with it. I loved that child with my whole heart and soul."
Looking straight into the camera, Patricia Ramsey addressed the killer, saying, "You may be eluding the authorites at this time but God knows who you are and we will find you."

According to reports, seven journalists were invited to meet with the Ramseys at a hotel in Boulder. The reporters were told to be in Boulder about 10 a.m. Thursday and were then called on their cellular phones and advised of the location of the secret meeting.
Several television news crews and still photographers also were permitted to attend the news conference and the footage was later made available to local TV stations and aired on CNN.
John Ramsey said the couple had been anxious to meet with the news media but he said the couple felt they had an obligation to talk to authorities before they talked to journalists.

Both parents met separately with two detectives and a representative of the Boulder County District Attorney's office on Wednesday, the first time in four months they had a formal interview with police.
John Ramsey said at first they were shocked and then outraged to be considered suspects in the crime.

"Then we understood statistically that is the sad state of affairs. We accepted being suspects. But what concerned us and still does is that any time spent looking at us (by police) is time that's wasted," he said.
The couple asked for the public's help in finding the killer of their 6-year-old daughter. Soon after the murder, the Ramseys put up a $100,000 reward for information leading to the killer.
"This ad with her most recent kindergarten picture will be appearing more frequently," said Patricia Ramsey, displaying an ad of JonBenet.

"We feel there are at least two people on the face of this earth who know who did it," she said, referring to the murderer and at least one confidant of the killer," she said without elaborating. "Please, please if you know anything, I beg you to call us," she said.
John Ramsey said an arrest is "absolutely necessary" for closure and looking for the killer would be "the sole mission for the rest of my life."
